summary:
A fast-moving grass fire at a Canadian military base killed four soldiers. The cause of the fire is still unknown, and Prime Minister Carney called it one of the worst peacetime tragedies for the Canadian military. The fire crossed established firebreaks before municipal firefighters helped contain it, and 19 other people were critically injured.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez submitted his resignation on Sunday, but President Emmanuel Macron refused it after weekend protests across France. Nuñez acknowledged that police lost control during the protests, and Macron admitted failures in anticipation and intelligence while criticising unbridled violence. Police have made 2,400 arrests across France. The Élysée palace said the resignation was submitted on Sunday.

Kenya's Ebola case count has reached eight, a senior health official said, while DR Congo's outbreak has spread to an eighth province. In DR Congo, two cases, including one death, were recorded in Nord-Ubangi, which borders the Central African Republic. The UN World Food Programme says funding shortfalls will force it to cut aid to about 500,000 people in Gaza, reducing monthly assistance from 1.6 million people to 1.1 million.

headlines.title: Grass fire at Canadian military base kills four soldiers
headlines.summary: Four soldiers were killed when a fast-moving grass fire swept through a Canadian military base. The cause remains unknown, and Prime Minister Carney called it one of the worst peacetime tragedies for the Canadian military.

headlines.title: Macron refuses interior minister's resignation after French protests
headlines.summary: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez submitted his resignation on Sunday, but President Emmanuel Macron refused it after nationwide protests. Nuñez acknowledged that police lost control, and police have made 2,400 arrests across France.

headlines.title: Ebola cases rise in Kenya and spread in DR Congo
headlines.summary: Kenya's Ebola case count has reached eight, a senior health official said, while DR Congo's outbreak has spread to an eighth province. Two cases, including one death, were recorded in Nord-Ubangi, which borders the Central African Republic.

headlines.title: World Food Programme to cut aid to 500,000 in Gaza
headlines.summary: The UN World Food Programme says funding shortfalls will force it to cut aid to about 500,000 people in Gaza. It is reducing monthly assistance from 1.6 million people to 1.1 million, in a territory where two thirds of the population is acutely food insecure.

headlines.title: Pope Leo greeted by crowds after lung cancer surgery
headlines.summary: Pope Leo XIV appeared in St Peter's Square for the first time since lung cancer surgery and pledged a gradual return to his duties. His surgeon said there is no clinical reason his South America trip cannot go ahead.

headlines.title: Independent MP Helen Haines critically injured in car attack
headlines.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines, 65, was deliberately struck by a car outside her Wangaratta office in regional Victoria and suffered critical injuries. A suspect is in custody, and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called it an attack.

headlines.title: Israeli police arrest suspects over settler attacks
headlines.summary: Israeli police arrested 10 suspects over settler attacks on a US journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank, though another report gave eight. The arrests followed calls by the United States, France, Belgium and Poland for Israel to take action.

headlines.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 election
headlines.summary: US President Donald Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection in Israel's October 27 election. Polls say Netanyahu and his far-right partners currently lack the majority needed to secure a new term.
